page0.text:
...I feel better, so maybe I'll go out for a while.
We still need to buy groceries for dinner, so I'll just hop over to the shopping district and be back before anyone knows it.

page1.text:
"Saber and Sakura are..."
Getting along just fine doing dishes.
I'd hate to interrupt their moment, so I'll just leave a note and slip out...

page2.text:
"Whew."
Somehow, I left without them noticing.
"Picking up food for dinner, back in an hour."
That's what I wrote on the note, so I should be fine.
If I pick up a 3 o'clock snack for them on the way back, that should be enough to calm their tempers, yeah.

page3.text:
"And...there."
With a bag full or groceries, I leave the supermarket Toyoetsu.
I didn't get much of a bargain on them, but I made sure to buy plenty of ingredients.
Now that Sakura's staying over, we'll have more mouths to feed.

page4.text:
"We had udon for lunch, so I think we'll have meat as the main course tonight."
I make my way home in high spirits, but something makes me stop.
"Hm?"
I can feel my clothes being pulled from behind.

page5.text:
"Huh...?"
I turn around curiously.
I'm met by the sight of
a young girl with silver hair.

page6.text:
"Wha—eh!?"
I leap backwards with a yelp.
The girl just watches as I panic.

page7.text:
"...?"
She doesn't seem hostile, much less murderous.
Instead, she says,
"I'm glad you're alive, big brother."
She beams at me in genuine joy.

page8.text:
"Wha..."
...There's no mistake that this is Berserker's Master.
She commands that monster that nearly tore me in half with a single slash that night.
She's from an ancient magical lineage that founded the Holy Grail War, which my old man Kiritsugu betrayed.
But what's she doing out here in the middle of the day?

page9.text:
...With Father Kotomine's words still fresh in my mind, she's no longer just a stranger to me.
That's why, without thinking, I murmur,
"Ill...ya?"
"Huh?"
Without knowing the significance of it, I blurt out the girl's name.

page10.text:
"Ah—no, I mean...!
Illyas—yeah, you're Illyasviel!
S-sorry I got your name wrong!"

page11.text:
I bow out of reflex.
It doesn't matter whether she's Berserker's Master or the daughter of the Einzberns right now.
I...just...
...can't leave her alone, not when she looks like she's about to cry.

page12.text:
"..."
"Ah, uh, I didn't mean anything bad by it. I just thought of your name, and..."

page13.text:
"...What's your name?"
"Huh?"
"Tell me your name, big brother. It isn't fair that only you know mine."
...
That's right, come to think of it.
Illyasviel introduced herself before, but I still haven't told her my name.

page14.text:
"I'm Shirou. Emiya Shirou."
"Emmy Yashiro? That's a weird name."
"No, you're saying it wrong. My family name is Emiya, and my given name is Shirou. If that's too hard, just use Shirou."
Without really thinking about it, I correct the girl's lilted pronunciation.

page15.text:
...
I even jab a reproachful finger at her, which makes her blink in surprise.

page16.text:
...
By the time I realize how blunt I'm being, it's too late.
Once again, she looks like she's about to cry.
"...Shirou. Shirou, huh? Okay, I like that.
It's simple, but it has a nice ring to it. Shirou suits you.
I'll let you off for being rude earlier!"
Suddenly, she grabs my arm.

page17.text:
"Whoa! H-h-hold on, Illyasviel! Whaddya think you're doing!?"
"It's okay, you can keep calling me Illya, Shirou! I'll call you Shirou, so we're even!"

page18.text:
"Wha... I mean, sure, that's easier to say, but wait!"
I try to shake Illya off my arm, but she just squeals in delight.

page19.text:
"Guh...!"
Uh-oh. At this rate, the neighborhood aunties will start to gossip.

page20.text:
"Damn it, what are you after!? Are you trying to hunt me down in broad daylight!?"
I finally wrench my arm out of her grasp.
...
...Ah.
Illya looks unhappy.

page21.text:
"W-what? Don't look at me like that. I don't know what you're doing here, but I'm a Master, too.
Illya shoots a glance at the shopping bag in my hand.
...But she also keeps looking at me curiously.

page23.text:
She's, um, not how I imagined.
...She laughed back then, too, but the feeling behind it was different, like maybe...
"...Illya. Did you not come here to fight?"
I timidly ask her.

page24.text:
"Why? Do you want me to kill you?"
"Mrgh."
Her gaze is enough to make my hair stand on end.
No matter how young she looks, this girl is the strongest Master.
She might be giggling innocently one second, and become a ruthless Master the next.

page25.text:
"...Hmm. I don't understand, but I'm fine with it if that's what you want. It'll just move up my schedule a little. Would you like to die here with Saber?"
"...Stop joking, of course not. I don't want to die, and I'd rather not fight here."

page26.text: "Right? Masters aren't supposed to fight while it's light out. You didn't bring Saber with you, and I didn't bring Berserker either."

page27.text:
"...Well, yeah. So what are you doing here? Did we just run into each other by chance?"
"Not by chance. I snuck away from Sella and came here to meet you. You should be honored."
Illya chuckles proudly.

page28.text:
...
I think I'm getting dizzy.
Just when I thought she was in serious Master mode, she's back to being an innocent child.
I have no way of knowing which side is the real Illya.

page29.text:
"...Fine. So you're here to see me.
But you're not here to fight...do I have that right?"
"Yeah. I'm here to talk to you, Shirou. You'll at least do that, will you? I've been waiting such a long time."
...
I don't know what she means by "at least," but apparently she really is just here to talk.

page30.text:
"Or do you not want to talk? ...If not, I'll just go home. I don't want to, but I don't like forcing people to do things."
Illya gazes up into my eyes.

page31.text:
"Ergh."
...As a Master, it's dangerous to stay here with Illya any longer. If Saber were here, I'm sure she'd be vehemently against this course of action.

page32.text:
...
...But I can't just leave, not when she's looking at me like that.
I know it's heedless, haphazard, and half-cocked, but...

page33.text: "I'm not against talking to you, Illya. To be honest, I've wanted to meet you, too."

page34.text:
"Yay! Then come this way! I found a small park earlier!"
As soon as I agree, Illya starts running, practically dancing in delight.

page35.text:
"Come on, hurry, or I'll leave you behind, Shirou!"
Illya runs off, dancing and twirling in innocent joy.

page36.text:
"I guess whatever happens, happens."
I resign myself to my fate and follow Illya.
Illya called me Shirou.
That means I should deal with her in kind, not as a Master, but a regular girl.

page37.text:
There's no one else at the park.
Not in the sandbox, nor on the swings.
It feels lonely. I sit down on a bench with Illya.

page38.text:
...We must look like an odd pair.
Illya's clearly not my sister since she's from overseas, but we have too much of an age gap to look like friends.

page39.text: "So, what did you want to talk about, Illya? You must have something to ask me."

page40.text:
"Why? I don't really have any questions for you."
...
Well, then.
How am I supposed to answer that, inscrutable little lady?

page41.text:
"...Illya. You're the one who said you wanted to talk.
But now you're saying there's nothing to talk about. Normally you wouldn't invite someone for a chat without business."
"Huh? R-really? We can't talk unless it's business...?"

page42.text:
"Ahh... That's not what I meant. I phrased that badly. We don't need to talk about business. Actually, it's more fun that way.
...But you've got me at a loss. I don't know you well, so I'm not sure what we should talk about. I don't know your likes or dislikes. That goes for you too, doesn't it? Wouldn't you feel uncomfortable if I suddenly asked you about things you wouldn't wanna talk about?"

page43.text:
"Mm... Yeah, maybe...but then what should I ask you? You won't get mad if I ask you anything I want?"
"Yeah, probably not. I'm the big brother here, so I'll try to act like a grown-up."
"Okay. Then, Shirou...do you like me?"

page44.text:
"Pfft!"
W-w-w-w-what does this kid think she's asking!?

page45.text:
"Ah, you're a liar. You said you wouldn't get mad, Shirou!"
"Anyone would be shocked by that, stupid! Y-you cut me in half, you know! I don't even know how to feel about that!"

page46.text: "That's not how it happened! You're the one who ran out in front even though you're so weak! I-it wasn't my fault!"

page47.text:
"The hell it wasn't! You showed up all ready to murder us! That's insane! And why does it matter whether I like you or not!?"
Illya's shoulders tremble, and she goes silent.

page48.text:
"Ah..."
...Oops.
I made up my mind to forget we're Masters, and here I am putting my foot in my mouth.

page49.text:
"Uh... Illya?"
"...Well, it matters to me. You're a jerk, Shirou, and you're all talk. You would've died if I didn't stop him."
Illya's shoulders shake and she stares at the ground, even as she says something ominous.

page50.text:
"...Haah."
...Well, she's got me there.
I'm the one who steered the conversation this way, and I'm older. Illya's just a kid.

page51.text:
"Ahem. Well, about that..."
I make up my mind and decide to say it.

page52.text:
"It's all in the past now, and I'm not hung up on it. You did let me go, and I'm all healed up now.
...Um, if it still bothers you, Illya, I won't ever mention it again. Is that all right?"

page53.text:
"Ah... Mm-hm. So you're not mad, Shirou...?"
"Nope. I should know better than to say this, but I'm not mad.
Right now, I'd like to talk to you more, Illya."

page54.text:
Her nearly tearful face suddenly turns into a smile.
...
Just seeing it brightens my mood, too.
Right now, Illya has no ill will towards me.
So I don't need to force myself to think like a Master.
As long as I've got her here, I'll have an easygoing chat with her, just like she wants.

page55.text:
I think Illya and I chatted for about an hour.
Illya happily listened as I talked about meaningless topics and everyday happenings.

page56.text:
...At some point, I realized how heartbreaking this was.
Illya really is an innocent little girl.
She doesn't hesitate when it comes to being a Master.
It's so tragic that she doesn't feel any fear about fighting in a war.

page57.text:
...
The magical lineage known as the Einzberns.
This young girl is who they sent to carry out their thousand-year-old obsession.

page58.text:
If that's Illya's objective too, then I...
"...Illya. Can I ask you something?"
"Hm? What?"
"Does the name Kiritsugu Emiya ring a bell?"
I just have to know.

page59.text:
...
Time stops.
It's an emotionless silence that seems to erase all the time we've spent together so far.

page60.text:
"No. I don't know anyone like that."
...Her silver hair sways.
Illya stands up from the bench and does a little twirl, like a fairy.

page61.text:
"It's almost sunset. Berserker will wake up once it's nighttime, so I should go home."
...
Illya bids me farewell in her childish way.

page62.text:
"Yeah. I better get home, too."
I stand up from the bench.
Break time is over.
The sun's setting, so we're back to being enemies.

page63.text:
And yet, I...
"Will we meet again, Illya?"
The question comes naturally to my lips.

page64.text:
"U-um, I'm not sure. I don't think so. Do you want to see me again, Shirou?"
"Yeah. I wouldn't ask unless I wanted to."
"...! Okay! Then I'll come find you tomorrow if I'm in the mood. Don't wait for me, though."
She runs out of the park.

page65.text:
But...
The pale girl stops awkwardly.

page66.text: "I lied earlier. I do know him."

page67.text:
"Illya...?"
"...I was born to win the Holy Grail War, but my goal is to kill you and Kiritsugu."

page68.text:
Her footsteps fade into the evening.
Leaving me with that, she leaves without looking back,
and I watch her go.
